blocks.text: Announcement
MFA, MA, and PhD Programs to Apply for by Early 2027
A list of arts-related graduate programs to explore and apply to before deadlines close.

blocks.alt: MFA, MA, and PhD Programs to Apply for by Early 2027

blocks.text: courtesy Chester Dale Collection, National Gallery of Art )

links.text: courtesy Chester Dale Collection, National Gallery of Art

blocks.text: These MFA, MA, and PhD programs are accepting applications now, with deadlines between December 2026 and February 2027. Many of the programs below are fully funded, with tuition waivers, stipends, and teaching assistantships.
Columbia University School of the Arts

The MFA in Visual Arts + Sound Art attracts emerging and mid-career artists from the United States and around the world to join a vibrant creative and intellectual community. Students are taught by internationally celebrated working artists in the city with the highest concentration of museums, galleries, nonprofit art spaces, independent collectives, and artist-run organizations. Deadline: January 20, 2027 | arts.columbia.edu
Cranbrook Academy of Art

Ranked among the United States’s top graduate-only programs in art, architecture, and design, Cranbrook prepares students to enter the industry with confidence. Up to 10 full-tuition fellowships and over 50 merit scholarships are available. Deadline: February 1, 2027 | cranbrookart.edu
Emily Carr University of Art + Design

As Canada's #1 university for art and design, ECU’s two-year MFA and MDes programs integrate creative exploration, research and critical inquiry, connecting you with faculty, industry and community partners to work on projects with real-world impact. The dedicated studio facilities, interdisciplinary research opportunities, and a collaborative graduate community allow students to push the boundaries of their practice to bring their ambitious ideas to life. Deadline: January 25, 2027 | ecuad.ca
Institute for Doctoral Studies in the Visual Arts

IDSVA offers a research-based, low-residency PhD in Visual Arts: Philosophy, Aesthetics, and Art Theory designed for artists, curators, writers, and creative thinkers. Through close mentorship with distinguished faculty and a globally engaged curriculum, students explore, question, and challenge how we understand art, culture, and human experience. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: December 7, 2026 | idsva.edu
Maine College of Art & Design

The Master of Fine Arts in Studio Art program in Portland, Maine, offers an interdisciplinary approach that encourages students to think across traditional academic boundaries, expand their art practice, and challenge their intellectual curiosity. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 17, 2027 | meca.edu
Massachusetts College of Art and Design

MassArt’s Graduate Assistantships support students’ interests and professional development beyond graduation. The assistantships are paid opportunities that build professional and academic experience while supporting teaching, research, studios, galleries, and administration. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 12, 2027 | massart.edu
Michigan State University

The three-year, customizable Interdisciplinary Studio MFA at this major research university is fully funded, with a stipend and additional fellowships. Students conclude the program with a thesis exhibition at the Broad Art Museum, the Zaha Hadid-designed landmark on campus. Deadline: January 5, 2027 | art.msu.edu
New York Studio School

NYSS’s full-time, two-year Master of Fine Arts program is a 60-credit degree centered on intensive, individual studio practice in drawing, painting, and sculpture. Rather than prescribing a single artistic direction, the program provides students with the time, space, and mentorship to pursue their own questions and cultivate their own distinctive artistic language. Deadline: January 15, 2027 | nyss.org
Otis College of Art & Design

Students receive access to painting, sculpture, and lighting studios; state-of-the-art wood and metal shops; photography, video, film, printmaking, and ceramics labs and 24/7 access to individual working studios. They are also guaranteed at least one semester of a Graduate Teaching Internship or Graduate Assistantship. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 15, 2027 | otis.edu
School of the Art Institute of Chicago

SAIC graduate programs, ranked among the top two independent art and design programs in the nation by US News and World Report , applaud experimentation and encourage students to cross disciplines and explore concepts unbound to any one medium or academic department in the realization of impactful work. Program offerings include MFA, MA, MArch, MDes, MS and Low-Residency MFA degrees, and a NEW MA in Curatorial Practices. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 10, 2027 | saic.edu
Sotheby's Institute of Art

Graduate students at Sotheby's examine the ideas, movements, and debates driving contemporary artistic practice, while building a deeper understanding of the global art ecosystem in which artists, curators, galleries, museums, and cultural institutions operate. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 20, 2027 | sothebysinstitute.com
Texas Christian University

MA and MFA graduate students receive full tuition funding, competitive stipends, and more. Students are trained for impactful careers in contemporary art, museums, and the broader arts field. Deadline: February 14, 2027 | finearts.tcu.edu
University of Arkansas

The School of Art, housed in the Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences, has four tuition-free graduate programs and offers graduate assistantships, stipends, and scholarships, as well as access to funding for fellowships, research and travel grants, and residencies. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 15, 2027 | uarkart.slideroom.com
University of Buffalo

The UB MFA is a two-year program in which students, faculty, visiting artists, and curators participate in an energetic, interdisciplinary dialogue around contemporary art. Students develop independent studio practices alongside thematic labs, research, academic electives, seminars, studio visits, group critiques, and exhibitions, while engaging with vibrant local and international arts communities. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 15, 2027 | arts-sciences.buffalo.edu
University of California, Davis

Supported by a $14 million endowment from Maria Manetti Shrem, the critically engaged Art Studio Program at UC Davis offers generous funding for incoming graduate students. With exceptional opportunities for fellowships and awards, the recently renamed Art Studio MFA provides students with spacious private studios so they can thrive in a vibrant, creative community as they work closely with internationally renowned faculty and visiting artists. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 5, 2027 | arts.ucdavis.edu
University of California, Los Angeles

The MFA in Media Arts at UCLA is a three-year program for artists working critically and experimentally with media, technology, and contemporary culture. Through studio practice, technical and theoretical seminars, group critiques, and individual tutorials with faculty, students develop ambitious bodies of work while questioning established ideas about art, technology, and what it means to be a media artist today. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 4, 2027 | dma.ucla.edu
University of Connecticut

The University of Connecticut’s (UConn) MFA in Studio Art is a funded, two-year graduate program combining advanced studio research with substantial undergraduate teaching experience. Located within a major research university, the program supports a broad range of practices, including painting, drawing, printmaking, bookmaking, sculpture, installation, and performance. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 15, 2027 | art.uconn.edu
University of Houston

Houston’s fully funded MFA offers concentrations in painting, photography, video, sculpture, graphic design, and interdisciplinary practices and emerging forms, as well as MA programs in Art History and Arts Leadership. Our state-of-the-art facilities, private studios with 24/7 access, dedicated exhibition spaces, research and project funds, paid internships, and world-renowned faculty empower you to launch your career from Houston, gateway of the Americas. Deadline: January 15, 2027 | uh.edu
University of Louisville

The rigorous 60-credit MFA program encourages experimentation, critical inquiry, and interdisciplinary exploration. Students may pursue interdisciplinary practices or concentrate on individual media, including ceramics, drawing, glass, painting, photography, printmaking, sculpture, design, new media, and installation. All MFA and MA students receive generous scholarships, with additional support for research, creative projects, and travel. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 15, 2027 | catalog.louisville.edu
University of Maryland, Baltimore County

The Intermedia and Digital Arts (IMDA) MFA Program invites applications from interdisciplinary artists seeking to expand or reinvent their practice. IMDA is a three-year, 60-credit graduate program with private studios in Baltimore’s progressive art community. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: February 1 2027 | imda.umbc.edu
University of Michigan

The University of Michigan’s Penny W. Stamps School of Art & Design, ranked #11 nationally among graduate art and design schools by U.S. News and World Report , is now accepting MFA in Art applications for Fall 2027. Graduates emerge prepared to exhibit internationally, secure tenure-track positions at leading institutions, create public art, and shape cultural organizations worldwide. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: January 3, 2027 | stamps.umich.edu
University of Notre Dame

Notre Dame offers full tuition waivers to all students admitted to the MFA degree in studio art or design. Additionally, a $29,000 stipend is awarded to all accepted students for each year of the program. Deadline: January 15, 2027 | artdept.nd.edu
Washington University in St. Louis

The MFA in Visual Art program is a two-year, fully residential program that supports diverse creativity — from historical techniques and emerging media to scholarly research and social practice. Read more on Hyperallergic Deadline: December 14, 2026 | samfoxschool.washu.edu
